note:
Your ask (9 Oct): speed up the jobs themselves, not only schedule them smarter. Using #130's timings, profile each job and make it faster. Focus on:
- Our hard resource limits, above all the NAS: batching; smarter ordering; fewer random reads and writes; its technical quirks (SMB takes ~20–55 small-file creates a second, so bulk goes as tar over SSH; fast sequential reads).
- Pure compute: algorithmic complexity and the code's execution (allocation, parallelism, SIMD, cache locality, memory-mapping instead of copying).

My additions to weigh:
- Work not done at all: inputs re-read or re-copied run after run that could be kept or shared; outputs rewritten unchanged; stages that could be skipped when their inputs are unchanged.
- Overlap: I/O and compute in the same job run one after the other where they could be pipelined (read the next area while computing this one).
- Downloads: tiles still fetched from AWS mid-job (peaks fetched dozens per area).
- Python steps that dominate a job, ported to Rust only where a profile shows it pays.
- Memory: peaks that force a job to run alone or swap.
- Each fix measured before and after on real areas, outputs proved byte-identical (or every difference explained), ranked by hours saved per full rebuild.

Needs #130. First look at where time goes: see #130's notes.
reply:
Done (9 Oct); the last batch publishing ~15:10 UTC. Every output byte-identical, no job keys changed.
- Where the time went (hours per full round): units 18 (mostly NAS), terrain 9.7, peaks 5.8, pack 4.2 (base-pack copying, not drawing), bldprep 4.3, trees 4.3.
- Terrain repair ~2.7× faster (pieces ~60 % less CPU; peaks' raw-tile work 57 % less); peaks' searches 2×.
- Units: neighbours' elevation samples read by slice and kept locally (11.5 → 7.7 GB for five units), the next unit's heritage slices, scenic results and building tiles fetched ahead; five adjacent units 4 min 44 s → 3 min 19 s warm.
- The build Mac keeps the base packs it just wrote (no 27-minute copy-back); catalog checks 2 min 23 s → 7 s; recipes read in parallel.
- Fixed: two places where outputs varied run to run; tree cover kept to its cores (#149).
- What's left, ranked, continues as #150.
text: Profile the build jobs and speed up the job code itself
